lede: (five report cards. four PASS on what the listing's Care line already says; one honest FAIL on the thing it says to keep away from.)
idea: The competitor corpus is full of 'waterproof' as a word and empty of it as evidence. So run the tests the customer runs anyway — shower, pool, sweat, sleeping in it, perfume — and file each as a report: condition, material, the Care line quoted verbatim, a result, and a rubber stamp. The fifth card fails on purpose: the listing says keep it away from perfume, so the card says spray first, then wear. Every row is the listing's own sentence; no durations or outcomes were invented.
type: The form is JetBrains Mono at 20/23px with dotted rules, the way a lab sheet is set; the condition line steps up to Jost 600. The Care line and notes rows switch to Cormorant italic because they are quotations. The stamp is Velista in oxblood at −9°, multiply-blended so it sits on the paper; FAIL is stamped in ink. The photograph is filed as FIG. n with a caption chip.
review: Pass 1: the stamp collided with the report date and the fig caption vanished on bright plates; the form was too thin and the middle third sat empty. Pass 2: date moved under the test number, caption given an ink chip, the italic remark moved under the form and a notes row added — the second half of the Care line, so the PASS cards also carry the perfume warning. Two frames were re-generated on fidelity: the slept-in hoop first came back as a two-strand twist instead of the listing's plait, and the half-in-half-out pool frame doubled the necklace.
verdict: the FAIL card is the one that will get screenshotted.

T1.title: Shower · pass
T1.why: Wrist and forearm under the stream, the steel spheres mirror-bright with water beading on every one, the gold heart hanging clear. The Care line covers it: waterproof and tarnish free, water is fine.
T1.check: mirror steel spheres (not pearls), gold toggle, gold heart; no face

T2.title: Pool · pass
T2.why: Fully submerged at the throat, caustics across the skin and the links, bubbles in the chain, the toggle shut at the front. The half-in-half-out variant was rejected because it rendered two necklaces.
T2.check: paperclip links, plain bar and ring, no stones, one necklace

T3.title: Sweat · pass
T3.why: Keep It On plate 07, approved 7 September: the 4mm chain on skin after a run. Tarnish free is the promise; sweat is daily wear.
T3.check: 4mm paperclip, toggle at front; approved plate

T4.title: Overnight · pass
T4.why: 06:40, the hoop still in, a pink pressure mark beside it on the lobe. The first render came back as a twisted rope; the second names the property — an open plait of five or six strands with over-under crossings — and holds.
T4.source: new generation fa6039d0 (497da977 rejected: twisted rope)
T4.check: plaited basket-weave, 25mm proportion, no stones, no eyes

T5.title: Perfume · fail
T5.why: An atomiser mid-spray on the left; the bracelet on folded linen well to the right, a clear gap of marble between. The listing's warning, stamped FAIL, and the useful advice: spray first, let it dry, then put it on. The variant with a hand was rejected for wearing rings and bangles that are not Naira's.
T5.check: three colours only, pavé halos, fold-over clasp, no gold
